title: A smooth algebra is a retract of a relative global complete intersection smooth over it
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then there are integers $n,c\ge0$ and polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that, writing $J=(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and $C=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/J$: (1) $C=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]; (2) the conormal module $J/J^2$, a $C$-module, is a free $C$-module with basis the classes $f_1\bmod J^2,\dots,f_c\bmod J^2$; (3) there are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\sigma:A\to C$ and $\pi:C\to A$ with $\pi\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_A$ such that $C$, an $A$-algebra via $\sigma$, is a smooth $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CG (lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection, line 567) and its proof (lines 580-588: Lemma 07CE lemma-improve-presentation gives A -> C with retraction; Algebra Lemma 07CF lemma-huber gives the presentation C = R[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_c) with the f_i mapping to a basis of J/J^2; fibre dimension n - c by Algebra Lemma 00SC lemma-lci). Stacks states 07CG for a syntomic ring map R -> A; this node is its case R -> A smooth (a smooth ring map is syntomic, Algebra Lemma 00TA lemma-smooth-syntomic), the only case used; clause (2) is the property of the presentation chosen in the proof, stated because Lemma 07CH uses it (the sequence 0 -> (+) C f_j -> (+) C dx_i).
